prompt: Without looking at any images, describe the most iconic image of Laughing Nailong (大笑奶龙 / 奶蛙) from memory: its pose, expression, body shape, colors, rendering style, and background, in enough detail for an artist who has never seen it to draw it. Say where you are unsure.
answer:
Important caveat: I don’t have a reliable memory of one canonical “most iconic” frame. “奶龙” is a 3D yellow baby-dragon character, and “大笑奶龙” is really a family of laughing stickers/emoji. “奶蛙” I remember only as an alternate nickname/variant, probably because the enormous laughing mouth makes him look frog-like; I am not confident that the canonical image is green. Treat the following as a reconstruction of the widely circulated laughing-sticker look, not a verified frame.

**Format and composition**
- Square sticker/emoji crop, character centered, filling most of the frame.
- Usually a bust or upper-body/three-quarter view; the huge face and open mouth are the subject. The lower body may be cropped or only suggested.
- Plain white or transparent background; at most a very soft pale-gray studio shadow. No scenery, no props, no text.

**Body shape**
- Chibi “baby dragon” proportions: an oversized, nearly spherical head sitting directly on a small pear/egg-shaped body, with almost no neck.
- Head is roughly as wide as the body and maybe 1.3–1.5 times its height; total character reads as about two head-heights tall.
- Body is round, soft, and pot-bellied, with a lighter cream oval belly patch.
- Limbs are very short and stubby: small rounded arms, short legs, flat rounded feet. No fingers beyond simple mitten-like nubs.
- Two small, rounded, slightly conical horn nubs on top of the head, set fairly wide apart. They should look soft, not sharp.
- A short tapered tail, usually curled to one side behind the body.
- Tiny vestigial wings may be present in the full dragon design, but in the laughing sticker they are not prominent; omit them or keep them as tiny rounded nubs behind the shoulders if you want the full “dragon” read. I am unsure how visible they are in the iconic crop.

**Expression**
- The defining feature is an enormous open-mouth laugh that takes up most of the lower half of the face, making the head look almost frog-like.
- Mouth: a wide, rounded trapezoid/oval, corners pulled far back and up, dark maroon-red interior, thick coral-pink tongue filling the lower part. No prominent teeth; if any, only two tiny rounded white upper teeth.
- Eyes: squeezed shut in delight, drawn as two thick black upward-bowed arcs, like “∩ ∩”, with no visible pupils. The cheeks push up into the eyes.
- Cheeks: large soft circular pink blush patches, one under each eye, partly outside the mouth corners.
- Nose: two tiny dark oval nostrils just above the mouth; no protruding snout.
- Overall expression: helpless, belly-laughing, delighted, slightly silly — not a polite smile.

**Pose**
- The version I recall most strongly is a standing/leaning-back laugh: body tilted back a little, belly pushed forward, head tipped up, feet planted apart and turned slightly outward.
- Arms are short and raised out to the sides, elbows bent, paws open, as if saying “ta-da” or mid-belly-laugh. An equally plausible variant has both hands resting on the belly; I am unsure which exact hand placement the most-shared frame uses.
- Legs slightly bent, giving a bouncing or wobbling look. Tail curled up behind.
- If drawing only the bust, keep the shoulders lifted and the head tilted back slightly; the body pose is secondary.

**Colors**
- Body: warm saturated banana/butter yellow, not neon; approximately #F6C945–#FFD24A.
- Belly/muzzle area: pale creamy yellow, approximately #FFF0B8.
- Horns: same yellow or slightly deeper amber.
- Blush: soft salmon/coral pink, semi-transparent.
- Mouth interior: deep wine/maroon, approximately #6E1E1E; tongue: coral pink #F06A7A.
- Eyes/linework: near-black, warm dark brown-black.
- I would not recolor him green for “奶蛙” unless you have a reference; in my memory the laughing image is yellow, and “奶蛙” is a nickname for the frog-like mouth rather than necessarily a green character.

**Rendering style**
- 3D cartoon render, like a soft vinyl/blind-box toy or an animation still: smooth matte surfaces, rounded bevels, soft global illumination, subtle specular highlights, no black outlines.
- Very little texture. The mouth interior is softly shadowed; the tongue has a slight glossy highlight. Eyes read as matte black beads or thick painted arcs.
- Lighting is bright, even, and flattering, with a gentle rim light to separate the yellow body from the white background.

**Where I am unsure**
- Whether the single most iconic image is a full-body standing laugh, a seated belly-laugh, or just the head/bust.
- Exact arm placement: raised to the sides vs. hands on belly.
- Whether the tail, wings, and horns are all visible in the iconic crop.
- Whether “奶蛙” means a green recolor, a frog-like nickname, or a separate character.
- Exact hex colors, number of teeth, and whether the background is pure white or transparent.

If an artist draws the oversized round yellow head, closed happy arc-eyes, huge maroon open mouth with pink tongue, pink cheek circles, stubby limbs, and soft 3D toy shading against a plain white ground, they will have the essential image even if the exact pose differs.
